verdict.catch: Space is the constraint, not custom. Prime rent runs near the top of Europe, so a trade only clears where the ticket is large enough to swallow the lease.

lenses.headline: Deep demand, no room.
lenses.read: London gives you customers and talent in abundance and makes you fight for the space to serve them.

scales.label: Demand depth
scales.sub: The spending pool is large and still rising.

scales.sub: Hiring is easy; keeping people is the cost.

income.read: Money runs deep and skews high. The everyday customer earns a solid wage, and a long tail above them leaves real room for a premium ticket.

space.prime_rent_note: Prime space runs near the top of Europe
space.read: Commercial space is the headline cost, and the terms tilt to the landlord. Budget the deposit and a long commitment; the short rent-free window is the only give.
space.peer_read: Against comparable European cities, London's rent sits at the top of the pack.
space.terms_read: Landlords want a long commitment and money down; a short rent-free window softens the fit-out.
space.terms_note: Standard on a prime retail unit; secondary streets soften every figure.

owner_runway._identity: runway = (rent_1bed + groceries + transport) x months(weeks_to_breakeven / 52 x 12) = $3,060 x 9 = $27,540 (~$28K)
owner_runway.read: Before the business pays you, you still have to pay to live. Plan the runway from the day you sign to the week the till clears costs.
owner_runway.runway_note: Personal burn only, not the business. Cut it by sharing rent or holding a part-time wage through fit-out.

demand_calendar.read: A summer hump, then a December peak. The swing is real but gentle; staff and stock for the festive lift, not a crisis.

trades.read: Take-home varies wide by trade, and the busiest trades are not the richest. What you keep matters more than what comes in.
trades.margin_read: Of every sale through the till, only a slim slice reaches the owner; rent and staff take the rest.

where_to_trade.read: The loud names pay a multiple of the city rent; a few quieter districts carry a far lighter load.

locals_intel.title: Business rates ride on top of rent.
locals_intel.detail: Headline rent understates the true cost by roughly a third once rates and service charge are counted. Price all three as one.

locals_intel.title: Footfall is postcode-deep.
locals_intel.detail: Two streets apart can halve trade. Stand outside the unit at the hours you plan to open before you sign.

locals_intel.title: Delivery trades carry road charges.
locals_intel.detail: Congestion and clean-air charges add up fast for anything on wheels. Budget them into the cost base.

character.read: The trading culture here is fast, card-first, and landlord-leaning. Plan for cards not cash, expect a slow first deal, and read every lease as the counterparty's document.

texture.takeaway: Do not plan for cash trade; price the card fees in.
Read the lease as the landlord's document, and negotiate the rent-free.
Licensing is exacting but predictable; start it early.
Suppliers and landlords move fast once trust is set.

peers.read: Against its peers London leads on reach and spend, and pays for it in rent.
